newsitem.title: USA: Appeals court upholds N.J. trash ruling -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Appeals court upholds N.J. trash ruling -- paper.

text.p: The U.S. Court of Appeals in Philadelphia has upheld most of a lower court ruling that New Jersey's waste management laws are unconstitutional, the Star Ledger reported Friday.
Whitman administration officials said they would appeal the ruling, but analysts said the effort was unlikely to succeed given a string of similar court rulings in recent years.

The state's system guarantees a steady stream of revenues to county-run waste facilities by forcing garbage haulers to deliver waste to in-state locations. But courts have ruled that violates the interstate commerce clause of the U.S. Constitution.
The state Assembly is considering bills that would allow counties to pay off bonds sold for the projects through a surcharge on local governments. But prospects for passage are uncertain.
